# 10 Times John Stewart Was The Most Powerful Green Lantern, Ranked
Sign in to your CBR account

Finally, John Stewart is making his live-action debut more than 50 years after his debut in *Green Lantern* Vol. 2 #87. Acclaimed actor Aaron Pierre, who is already a veteran of DC Comics adaptations after starring on the SyFy series *Krypton* as Dev-Em, is portraying the superhero alongside Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan in the upcoming DC Universe TV show, *Lanterns*.
This is a long time coming for the first Black Green Lantern Corps member, created by writer Dennis O'Neil and artist Neal Adams in the early 1970s, who almost appeared in *Zack Snyder's Justice League* before his scene was deleted.
In fact, it is hard to believe he has not had the honor of a live-action portrayal sooner, given how many moments from the comics and on animated television shows have proven that he was one of the most powerful people, if not the most powerful person, to wield the Green Lantern ring.
## John Stewart Prevents A Horrific Train Crash
While the likes of Hal Jordan, Guy Gardner and others would come before him, for superhero fans who grew up in the early 2000s, John Stewart is considered the definitive Green Lantern. A great deal of credit for this reputation can be attributed to his involvement in the beloved animated series, *Justice League*, in which he is played by prolific voice actor Phil LaMarr.
One episode sees John use his ring to grab hold of a commuter train that nearly derails after a brake malfunction. He is, unfortunately, unable to stop the runaway vehicle from crashing into the station, but the damage would have been much worse and resulted in many fatalities had he not intervened.
## John Stewart Leads The Lost Army Of Lanterns
John Stewart is, above all things, a great, natural-born leader. He has the know-how and the courage to guide others through thick and thin and into the most dangerous and mysterious territories imaginable, always coming out on the other side with his people intact.
One important instance in which his leadership skills were most needed was during the events of the 2015 storyline, *Green Lantern: The Lost Army*, by Cullen Bunn and Jesús Saíz. In the series, considered one of the most essential John Stewart stories, the Emerald Knight becomes the only hope to rescue a group of Green Lanterns who have become stranded in uncharted corners of deep space.
## John Stewart Refuses To Conceal His Identity
John Stewart made it clear that he was going to be a Green Lantern unlike any to come before him in his first DC Comics appearance. It was not even a heroic deed or a special trick with his ring that proved it, but a simple decision that made him stand out.
Fellow Earth-born Green Lantern Hal Jordan hands the recruit a mask to wear, just like he does to keep his identity a secret. However, Stewart tells him that he does not need it because he has nothing to hide, which is, to put it simply, super cool.
## John Stewart Wields The Dark Star Ring
In 2024, DC Comics had pretty much already confirmed that John Stewart was the most powerful Green Lantern in the universe. However, he would soon become one of the universe's most powerful beings, period, after acquiring another enchanted object.
In *Green Lantern: War Journal #11*, by Phillip Kennedy Johnson, Montos, Adriano Lucas, and Dave Sharpe, John's conflict with the Old God called Olgrun and his Radiant Dead eventually leads him to come into possession of the Dark Star Ring, which grants the wielder greater power than any other ring in existence. Of course, the responsibility of preventing that power from falling into the wrong hands is up to him.
## John Stewart's Architectural Expertise Defeats Olgrun
In between his careers as a U.S. Marine and a Green Lantern, John Stewart made a living as an architect. On a few occasions, his skills in this field would actually end up proving effective in his bid to protect the universe from cosmic chaos.
Imbued with the power of the Dark Star ring, John rebuilds the long-destroyed Necropolis, which traps Olgrun and his realm inside, preventing him and his army of the Radiant Dead from wreaking havoc on the universe. If not for his experience as an architect, he might not have thought of this solution to one of his most catastrophic conflicts yet.
## John Stewart Saves Batman And Martian Manhunter
John Stewart using his ring to save Batman and Martian Manhunter on Justice League

John Stewart using his ring to save Batman and Martian Manhunter on Justice League

Image via Warner Bros. Animation / DC
Few would disagree that John Stewart was the right choice to represent the Green Lantern Corps on *Justice League*. That argument was settled from the moment Phil LaMarr's take on the role first appeared on the animated series.
In the show's pilot episode, Batman (Kevin Conroy, arguably the best Batman voice actor ever) and Martin Manhunter (Carl Lumbly) are battling an alien enemy from inside the Batwing when it becomes damaged mid-air. The heroes could have tumbled to an almost certain death if John had not stepped in and used his ring to bring the aviary vehicle to safety.
## John Stewart Persuades General Zod
If there is one tool more powerful than the Green Lantern ring, or even the Dark Star ring, it is the power of persuasion. Such is a skill that John Stewart also possesses, and would use brilliantly to his advantage when attempting to join forces with General Zod.
The rogue Krytonian dictator sees the Green Lantern Corps as an enemy, believing they, specifically a corps member named Tomar-Re, are responsible for his planet's destruction. John, after besting him in a fight with Kryptonite knuckles, manages to convince Zod to help him defeat Tomar-Re's son, Tomar-Tu.
This instantly iconic moment from *Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps* #45 is living proof of John's claim that he wins his battles "before they're fought."
## John Stewart Lures His Green Lantern Ring Toward Himself
The true test of a person's worth to join the Green Lantern Corps is their capability as a warrior, even without the power of the ring. John Stewart has proven that time and time again over the years, though it was especially clear in an episode of *Justice League*.
John and Hawkgirl (Maria Canals-Barrera) are being held captive and incapacitated by Despero (Keith David) when the three-eyed alien begins torturing her. To put a stop to it, John manages to telekinetically bring his Green Lantern ring onto his finger, allowing him to free himself and his teammate and take down the ruthless villain.
## John Stewart Makes An Impossible Sniper Shot
As previously mentioned, John Stewart's experience protecting the universe as part of the Green Lantern Corps is preceded by his experience protecting the United States of America as a Marine. His specialty was long-range precision marksmanship, otherwise known as "sniping," which would prove to be yet another skill that would come in handy during his cosmic escapades.
In *Green Lantern Corps Special #1, Vol. 1*, the planet Oa is under attack by a Sinestro Corps member named Bedovian, who is mowing down Lanterns with his expert sniper abilities. Luckily, John Stewart is able to give Bedovian a taste of his own medicine by successfully hitting him with a sniper shot from a distance of about three space sectors, which is roughly three full galaxies away.
This is more than enough to prove that John is, without a doubt, the most skilled man in the universe behind a sniper rifle.
## John Stewart Becomes A Guardian Of The Universe
John Stewart becomes a Guardian of the Universe

John Stewart becomes a Guardian of the Universe

Image via DC Comics

Being a member of the Green Lantern Corps, let alone the first Black person to be recruited into the group, is just one of many honors that John Stewart can claim to have. For instance, one of his most esteemed achievements would be depicted in the early 1990s release of *Green Lantern: Mosaic*.
The miniseries saw the beginning of John Stewart's brief tenure as a member of the Guardians of the Universe, which is a race of immortal beings who are responsible for the creation of the Green Lantern Corps. In other words, he was given a pretty amazing promotion that no other mortal person before him ever had the honor of receiving.
When Lanterns debuts for the DCU on HBO Max, the timeline for John Stewart and Hal Jordan won't be what many expect.
